title: Simulation of Register Halving
statement: Let a program have finitely many natural-number registers, labels in a set $\Lambda$, and an oracle for its calls. Suppose its instruction at label $l$ is to replace register $r$ by its integer quotient upon division by $2$ and continue at label $l'$. For any Boolean input $x$, initial register values $v$, output word, and integer bound $W$ with the length of the binary word for $v(r)$ at most $W$, the compiled program can run from the configuration with label $l$, registers encoded by their binary words, all work heads at cell $0$, and the given output to the corresponding configuration with label $l'$, register $r$ set to $\lfloor v(r)/2\rfloor$, and the other registers and output unchanged. During this finite run, every earlier configuration has no pending oracle call, and every work head position lies between $-1$ and $W$, inclusive.
